title: Infinite ergodic theory and functional statistics of non-confined Feller process
abstract: We study additive observables of a non-confined Feller process characterized by a non- normalizable stationary probability density and return times with infinite mean. The process is equivalent, after a deterministic rescaling, to a squared Bessel process, but we focus here on a question: the spatial structure of its local-time field. We show that the local time admits a fac- torization in the long time limit. Its spatial profile is governed by the non-normalizable stationary density, whereas its temporal fluctuations are controlled by a single Mittag-Leffler random ampli- tude. As a consequence, normalized spatial correlations of the local time converge to a universal constant independent of the two observation levels. Occupation times of finite intervals follow as corollaries and display Darling-Kac fluctuations. In contrast, non-integrable power observables exhibit self-similar squared-Bessel-type limits rather than Mittag-Leffler statistics. This spatial- field perspective provides a unifying framework for infinite ergodic theory under state-dependent multiplicative noise.
summary: This paper investigates the long-time statistical behavior of non-confined Feller processes, which exhibit infinite ergodic behavior due to non-normalizable stationary densities. The key finding is that the local-time field factorizes into a deterministic spatial part and a random temporal part governed by Mittag-Leffler statistics. This provides a unifying framework for understanding correlations in systems where standard ergodicity breaks down.
main_problem: The study focuses on the spatial structure and multi-point correlation properties of the local-time field for non-confined Feller processes within the framework of Infinite Ergodic Theory.
main_result: The local-time field exhibits an asymptotic spatiotemporal factorization, $L(x, t) \propto I(x) \cdot \xi$, where the spatial profile is deterministic and the temporal fluctuations are governed by a Mittag-Leffler random amplitude.
method: The analysis uses asymptotic factorization techniques, comparing the non-confined (infinite ergodic) regime to the standard ergodic regime, and analyzing scaling limits for various observables.
model_or_system: The model is a non-confined Feller process, which is characterized by a non-normalizable stationary probability density, contrasting with confined cases where standard ergodic theory applies.
key_observables: Local-time field $L(x, t)$, normalized spatial correlations of local time, occupation times ($T_a(t)$), and non-integrable power observables ($A_q(t)$).

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of an infinite invariant density $I(x)$ when standard ergodicity breaks down.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the Feller process in both confined and non-confined settings, reviewing the transition from standard to infinite ergodic theory, and then detailing the results on local-time factorization, correlation functions, and the distinction between integrable and non-integrable observables.
why_interesting: The concept of infinite ergodic theory and the resulting Mittag-Leffler statistics provide powerful tools for analyzing systems where standard time-averaging theorems fail, which is relevant for non-equilibrium dynamics in complex physical systems.
